findings.evidence: mathlib grep: `Module.Finite.toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_surjective ... Function.Surjective (Module.toModuleEnd (End R M) (S := R) M)`; `Module.Invertible.toModuleEnd_bijective : Function.Bijective (toModuleEnd R (S := R) M)`.
findings.fix: Rename to `toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_bijective` to match the adjacent `toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_surjective` it strengthens.
findings.issue: `toModuleEnd_bijective` sharpens `Module.Finite.toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_surjective` (Mathlib/RingTheory/SimpleModule/Basic.lean:581) — the exact same map `R →+* Module.End (Module.End R M) M` — but drops the second `moduleEnd`, breaking the surjective→bijective naming correspondence. The bare name also already exists in Mathlib as `Module.Invertible.toModuleEnd_bijective` (PicardGroup.lean:255) for the unrelated map `R → Module.End R M`, so the short name is overloaded onto two different statements.

findings.evidence: Same map `Module.toModuleEnd (Module.End R M) M (S := R)` as the surjectivity lemma named with `toModuleEnd_moduleEnd`.
findings.fix: Rename to `toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_bijective_of_isSimpleRing` for consistency with the surjective lemma and the renamed base theorem.
findings.issue: `toModuleEnd_bijective_of_isSimpleRing` inherits the same stem mismatch as `toModuleEnd_bijective`.

summary: The main theorem name drops the second `moduleEnd` stem of the Mathlib lemma it directly sharpens and reuses a name Mathlib already assigns to a different map. Other names are fine.
